text: Thus explained in sequence, through the practice of analyzing the twenty-five principles, knowledge arises in the Purusha: "This is Nature, this is the Purusha, and these are the five subtle elements, the senses, and the gross elements." [The Purusha realizes], "It is not so; I do not become this; this body is not mine; since I am distinct and the body is distinct, I am not the body." Thus, [this knowledge] becomes free from the residue of ego and, being devoid of distortion, becomes completely pure. Distortion is doubt; therefore, without distortion, it is without doubt and completely pure. [The realization is], "Only that exists, nothing else." Thus, the cause of liberation arises and is manifested—the knowledge, the knowledge of the twenty-five principles of the Purusha.
